behavioral_effects: message-item.tsx sets data-role on the message wrapper
chat.spec asserts the assistant marker for a reply, and progress-or-reply after sending; auth.spec user-menu locator takes .first()
compatibility_impact: Every chat message wrapper now carries data-role=user|assistant; nothing else reads it. The loading-state spec is renamed to describe what it asserts.
follow_up: Watch the e2e job on this push; if the MCP OAuth callback redirect still flakes at its 5 second URL budget, widen that assertion in its own session
limitations: Fix-forward on the e2e job after its first full run: 29 passed, 1 failed, 3 flaky - all four traced to spec assumptions, not to the stack
reason: The first composed-stack e2e run showed the fake model replying immediately, which exposed three spec assumptions that only held with a slow real model: the chat specs waited for a data-role marker the message component never rendered or for a transient thinking state that never became visible, and the user-menu spec used a strict-mode locator that matches twice for a user with no display name. After this change the message wrapper carries data-role, the chat specs assert on the reply or on progress, and the user-menu spec takes the first match.
security_impact: None. A data attribute on a client component and three spec locators.
summary: Mark chat messages with data-role and make the e2e chat and user-menu assertions hold when the model answers instantly

validators_run.evidence_ref: against the local docker frontend (35 hours old, without data-role) the send-and-receive spec fails as expected; a host dev server on 3100 could not be driven because dev-mode cold compiles exceed the setup project's 10 second redirect budget. The CI e2e job on this push, which uses the production build, is the validation
